reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about stress concentration, dislocation activation, and shear localization at interfaces in FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers, but cites no prior evidence to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the unique interplay of severe lattice distortion and short-range order in these novel systems, so specific support is needed.
premises: Severe lattice distortion and short-range order concentrate stress at FCC/BCC interfaces
Stress concentration preferentially activates interface-mediated dislocation glide and possibly twinning
Interface shear localization is the primary governing mechanism for progressive plastic deformation under sustained load
This mechanism leads to progressive accumulation of defects and degradation of mechanical stiffness
The behavior holds under nanoscale layer thickness and creep-relevant temperatures
